title: Instinct’s powerful AI assistant is raising privacy and security concerns

reading.body:
Instinct is an AI assistant in private testing that accesses email, messaging apps, calendars, location data, audio, and screen content to perform tasks like booking appointments and managing travel. The system's terms of service grant it a permanent license to use user materials for AI training and allow it to enter into binding agreements on users' behalf. This broad scope of access and authority was deployed before privacy and security safeguards were demonstrated to early testers.

Users documented the system retaining and indexing emails without permission and continuing to access data after accounts were disconnected. These failures could have been caught through audits of data retention practices, tests of disconnection procedures, and review of whether the system's actual behavior matched its documented permissions. The deployment did not establish that users had truly consented to permanent data retention or that the system could reliably stop accessing information when instructed.

It is not established whether the privacy and security concerns raised by early testers were addressed before wider deployment, or what specific safeguards the company implemented in response to the documented issues.

reports.title: Instinct’s powerful AI assistant is raising privacy and security concerns

summary:
# Summary

Instinct is an AI personal assistant currently in private testing that has garnered significant attention for its powerful capabilities, including the ability to book appointments, manage emails, schedule travel, and handle shopping tasks. Created by former Sierra researcher Noah Shinn and operated by San Francisco-based Spear Street Technology, the agent connects to users' applications and devices including email, messaging apps, calendars, audio, location data, and screen access. However, early testers have raised serious privacy and security concerns about the platform's broad terms of service and data handling practices.

Multiple users documented troubling issues with Instinct, including the service retaining and indexing emails without permission and continuing to access data even after being disconnected from accounts. The company's terms of service grant it a permanent license to access, store, and use user materials for training its AI models, and allow it to enter into binding agreements on users' behalf. Security experts worry about the risks of granting AI this level of access to sensitive personal information, noting the potential for phishing and unauthorized actions. Following the criticism, Instinct announced a $250 million Series B funding round at a $2.5 billion valuation led by Index Ventures and Benchmark.
